av_event.line_text: I just clicked on stuff till it went away, to be honest.
av_event.what: An older woman (Kerry's mum) walks into the kitchen behind Kerry, fills the kettle at the counter and switches it on, then walks back out of frame; the kettle starts to rumble faintly on the audio.

text:
A: Alright! Can you hear me? I'm Liam.
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Kerry. You're loud, aren't you?
A: Ha, my mum says that every single day. Where are you, then?
B: Bridgwater. Somerset.
A: Nice one. I'm Ilkeston, between Nottingham and Derby. I'm a sparky, domestic mostly, bit of commercial. Got a job tomorrow where the last bloke's done proper cowboy wiring, junction boxes just buried in the plaster, no labels, nothing. I'll be there all day, you know?
B: My son's doing mechanics at college. He'd love all that, taking stuff apart.
A: Good lad. Get a trade, that's what I say. Nobody can take it off you. I'm going self-employed in a couple of years, EV chargers and solar, that's where the money is now. My own van, name on the side, the lot.
B: Fair play. Is it a lot of paperwork, that, going on your own?
A: Er, a bit, yeah. You get an accountant, don't you. Sorts itself out.
B: That's the bit I couldn't be doing with. They asked me about team leader at work and I thought, no, all them forms.
A: What do you do?
B: Tills, and the customer service desk at the big supermarket. I've just come off a shift actually.
A: You look it, no offence.
B: Cheers.
A: Nah, I mean that nicely! I'm shattered most days myself. I went bouldering last night and my arms are still dead, I can barely lift a cob.
B: Oh, you say cob as well! The teacher I just talked to said that. I thought she was having me on.
A: It's a cob, mate. What else would it be?
B: A roll! A bread roll!
A: Nah, sorry, but that's wrong. Anyway, what were that puzzle about at the start? I flew through it.
B: I just clicked on stuff till it went away, to be honest.
A: Ha, fair. So what do you do for fun down there?
B: Carnival. Bridgwater Carnival, it's in November. The floats are massive, all lit up, thousands of bulbs. I help my cousin's club with theirs. Best night of the year, I've been every year since I was a toddler.
A: That sounds sick, actually. I take photos of that sort of thing, street art, old factories, murals. There's a mural in Sneinton I've been back to like five times. Have you been to Nottingham Contemporary?
B: No. I don't really get modern art, to be honest. Half of it's a con. A pile of bricks and they want a grand for it.
A: Nah, see, that's what everyone says, but you've got to actually look at it. Your carnival floats are basically art, aren't they?
B: That's different. That's people building something.
A: That's what an artist does! Mate, you was halfway to agreeing with me there.
B: I wasn't. Do you go away much, then?
A: City breaks. Berlin's my favourite, the clubs over there, the murals, unreal. Budapest, Lisbon, Amsterdam. I want Japan next, or Mexico City.
B: I did Tenerife for my fortieth. Too hot, and full of English people moaning anyway. I'm happy in a caravan at Brean.
A: Brean! Nah, I'd go mad by day three. I need a bit of buzz, you know?
B: Well, Callum would probably agree with you. He'd be off to Berlin tomorrow if I let him.
A: Let him go, mate! Best thing I ever...
